articles.headline: Fraunhofer IPA Develops Stable Aluminum Anodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries
articles.dek: Researchers have created a new technology to manage volume changes in aluminum anodes, paving the way for their use in practical battery applications.
articles.lead: Fraunhofer IPA, in collaboration with the University of Stuttgart, has announced a breakthrough in battery technology with the development of a new cell and electrode system for aluminum anodes. This innovation addresses a significant challenge that has previously hindered the widespread adoption of aluminum in lithium-ion batteries.
articles.takeaway: Researchers have created a new technology to manage volume changes in aluminum anodes, paving the way for their use in practical battery applications.
body: Fraunhofer IPA, in collaboration with the University of Stuttgart, has announced a breakthrough in battery technology with the development of a new cell and electrode system for aluminum anodes. This innovation addresses a significant challenge that has previously hindered the widespread adoption of aluminum in lithium-ion batteries.

The primary issue with aluminum anodes has been their tendency to undergo substantial volume changes during the charging and discharging cycles. These fluctuations can lead to instability and reduced battery lifespan, making them impractical for many applications.

The newly developed technology aims to stabilize these volume changes, making them manageable for practical battery use. By controlling the expansion and contraction of the aluminum anode, the researchers have overcome a key obstacle.

This advancement could have significant implications for the future of energy storage, potentially leading to more efficient and cost-effective batteries for various applications, including electric vehicles.

attribution.originalTitle: Fraunhofer stabilises aluminium anodes for lithium-ion batteries

faqs.question: What problem does the new Fraunhofer IPA technology solve?
faqs.answer: The technology stabilizes the volume changes that occur in aluminum anodes during charging and discharging cycles.

faqs.question: What is the potential impact of this development?
faqs.answer: It could enable the practical use of aluminum as an anode material in lithium-ion batteries, potentially leading to more efficient and cost-effective energy storage solutions.

articles.headline: EU-UK Trade Rules for Electric Vehicle Batteries to Take Effect in 2027
articles.dek: New 'Made in Europe' rules for electric vehicle batteries under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement are set to be implemented as planned in January 2027, despite industry calls for delays.
articles.lead: The European Union and the United Kingdom's Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA) includes rules of origin for electric vehicle (EV) batteries, which are crucial for tariff-free trade. These regulations, set to take effect on January 1, 2027, stipulate that battery packs and cells must originate in the EU or UK, with a limit of 30-35% non-originating content for cathode active materials.
articles.takeaway: New 'Made in Europe' rules for electric vehicle batteries under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement are set to be implemented as planned in January 2027, despite industry calls for delays.
body: The European Union and the United Kingdom's Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA) includes rules of origin for electric vehicle (EV) batteries, which are crucial for tariff-free trade. These regulations, set to take effect on January 1, 2027, stipulate that battery packs and cells must originate in the EU or UK, with a limit of 30-35% non-originating content for cathode active materials.

Automakers, represented by the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association (ACEA), have been pushing for a further delay to these rules, which have already been postponed by three years. However, an analysis by Transport & Environment (T&E) debunks the industry's claims and supports the implementation of the existing regulations.

T&E's findings indicate that EU battery production capacity will significantly exceed the demand required for EU-UK trade in 2027. For nickel-rich NMC batteries, EU production is projected to be six times the amount needed for exports to the UK, and for lithium-iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, it will be 2.4 times the requirement.

Furthermore, the analysis shows sufficient cathode active material (CAM) production within the EU to meet the demand for EU-built EVs exported to the UK. EU CAM supply is expected to surpass the needs for both NMC and LFP batteries by over a third, and by nearly five times for NCA batteries.

Implementing these rules is considered vital for securing Europe's battery value chain and maintaining investor confidence. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič has previously stated that the Commission would introduce a mechanism to prevent further extensions beyond 2032, emphasizing the need for the permanent TCA rules of origin to apply as scheduled.

attribution.originalTitle: EU-UK TCA: Getting Made in Europe Rules Right

faqs.question: What are the key requirements for EV batteries under the EU-UK TCA?
faqs.answer: Battery packs and cells must originate in the EU or UK, with a maximum of 30-35% non-originating content for cathode active materials.

faqs.question: What is the projected EU battery production capacity for 2027?
faqs.answer: EU battery production capacity is expected to far exceed the demand from EU-UK trade, with significant surpluses for NMC, LFP, and NCA battery types.

articles.headline: Africa Urged to Process Critical Minerals, Avoid Oil Era Mistakes
articles.dek: Former Nigerian oil executive Bala Wunti warns that Africa risks repeating past economic pitfalls by exporting raw critical minerals instead of processing them domestically.
articles.lead: Bala Wunti, who has extensive experience in Nigeria's oil sector, cautioned African nations at the 2026 Concordia Annual Summit against repeating the economic mistakes made during the crude oil era with the continent's new mineral wealth. He argued that exporting raw materials like lithium, cobalt, and rare earth elements, while importing refined products, leads to poverty rather than prosperity.
articles.takeaway: Former Nigerian oil executive Bala Wunti warns that Africa risks repeating past economic pitfalls by exporting raw critical minerals instead of processing them domestically.
body: Bala Wunti, who has extensive experience in Nigeria's oil sector, cautioned African nations at the 2026 Concordia Annual Summit against repeating the economic mistakes made during the crude oil era with the continent's new mineral wealth. He argued that exporting raw materials like lithium, cobalt, and rare earth elements, while importing refined products, leads to poverty rather than prosperity.

Wunti highlighted that global energy is shifting from being priced in barrels of oil to kilograms of battery minerals. He emphasized that processing capacity, not just raw deposits, is becoming the key driver of economic advantage in this new landscape.

Drawing parallels to the oil industry, Wunti stated that Africa must evolve into a processing partner for its critical minerals, rather than remaining solely a source of raw materials. He described the permanent export of unrefined minerals as a form of "colonial economics," though he acknowledged that temporary concentrate exports might sometimes be commercially necessary.

Nigeria's own situation serves as an example, with the country having identified 44 critical minerals. However, Wunti pointed out that geological indications do not equate to proven reserves backed by internationally recognized data, and investors fund projects, not potential.

His experience includes leading the renegotiation of Nigeria's Deep Offshore Production Sharing Contracts, which resolved a two-decade stalemate with international oil companies and secured a greater share of offshore revenue for the government.

attribution.originalTitle: Africa: Wunti Warns Africa Against Repeating Its Oil Mistake

faqs.question: What is the main concern Bala Wunti has for Africa's mineral wealth?
faqs.answer: Bala Wunti is concerned that Africa might repeat the economic mistakes of its oil era by exporting raw critical minerals instead of processing them domestically.

faqs.question: Why is processing capacity important for Africa's critical minerals?
faqs.answer: Processing capacity is becoming the primary source of economic advantage as global demand for battery minerals rises, and it allows African nations to gain more value from their resources.

This is a notable accomplishment for a young company in the capital-intensive electric motorcycle sector. Vammo is also introducing its third-generation swapping stations, which are designed to reduce costs by an additional 15% through AI-powered software that optimizes battery charging based on demand and usage patterns.

Despite electric motorcycles accounting for only 0.7% of Brazil's motorcycle sales, Vammo claims over 65% of the domestic electric motorcycle market. articles.takeaway: A new charging facility in Ontario, California, aims to support the growing demand for electric big rigs in the region's key logistics and freight hub.
body: EV Realty has announced plans for a new electric semi-truck charging hub in Southern California's Inland Empire. The site, located at 2151 E. Philadelphia Street in Ontario, is situated in a major warehousing and logistics area.

The new hub is strategically positioned with access to major freeways, including the SR-60 and I-15, and is designed to serve fleets operating in the region. Its location is intended to support operations for the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, as well as intermodal facilities and Ontario International Airport.

EV Realty CEO Patrick Sullivan stated that the Ontario location is at the convergence of a major container gateway and a dense warehouse cluster, calling it an epicenter for truck electrification in the United States. He added that once operational, EV Realty will have 27 MW of simultaneous truck charging capacity in the area.

Construction at the site is expected to begin early next year, with the charging facility anticipated to be operational before 2028. The company highlighted the need for high-capacity charging sites in Southern California due to constrained grid capacity in many areas.

articles.lead: BYD has produced its 150,000th new energy commercial vehicle, a Q3 electric semi truck, at its plant in Huai’an, Jiangsu province. This milestone highlights BYD's growing presence in the commercial vehicle sector, complementing its established battery and passenger car businesses.
articles.takeaway: The company's Q3 electric semi truck, featuring an 800 hp powertrain and 600 kWh battery, represents a significant step in BYD's expansion into the heavy-duty electric vehicle market.
body: BYD has produced its 150,000th new energy commercial vehicle, a Q3 electric semi truck, at its plant in Huai’an, Jiangsu province. This milestone highlights BYD's growing presence in the commercial vehicle sector, complementing its established battery and passenger car businesses.

The Q3 electric semi truck is equipped with BYD's blade-style lithium iron phosphate batteries, totaling 600 kWh. Its dual-motor system delivers approximately 800 horsepower, designed to haul up to 108,000 lbs. The truck offers a range of over 200 miles on a single charge.

To minimize downtime, the Q3 supports dual-gun DC fast charging, capable of reaching an 80% state of charge from 20% in just 30 minutes. This rapid charging capability is crucial for fleet operators looking to integrate electric trucks into their operations.

BYD's New Energy truck business has seen substantial growth, with 6,848 NEV trucks sold in September alone, an increase of 113.33% year-over-year. Through the first nine months of 2026, the company delivered 53,032 units, marking a 28.46% rise compared to the same period in 2025.

body: Across hundreds of procurement records and very different transit markets, battery-electric has become the reference technology for zero-emission bus fleets. Support CleanTechnica's work through a Substack subscription, on Patreon, or on Stripe.
Help us produce all of the high-quality, original content we publish week after week despite the challenges of content-scraping AI, antisocial media, inflation, and other hurdles.

Zero-emission bus procurement has moved beyond the stage where battery-electric and hydrogen fuel-cell buses should be treated as two parallel technologies waiting for the market to decide between them.

Transit agencies have now spent years operating both, rebuilding depots, installing charging and refuelling infrastructure, training technicians and discovering which assumptions survive daily service.
Both technologies can move passengers without tailpipe emissions. The more useful evidence now comes from what agencies are prepared to buy repeatedly and at fleet scale.
I assembled a global procurement register with 388 sourced records across 81 countries, separating firm orders and awards from tenders, options, framework quantities and funding announcements.

articles.headline: Volkswagen Group Unveils Four Affordable Electric Urban Cars
articles.dek: CUPRA Raval, Volkswagen ID. Polo, Škoda Epiq, and Volkswagen ID. Cross debut together, attracting nearly 150,000 orders.
articles.lead: The Volkswagen Group has presented its Electric Urban Car Family (EUCF) for the first time as a complete lineup at the Paris Motor Show. This family includes the CUPRA Raval, Volkswagen ID. Polo, Škoda Epiq, and Volkswagen ID. Cross, all built on the MEB+ Platform.
articles.takeaway: CUPRA Raval, Volkswagen ID.
body: The Volkswagen Group has presented its Electric Urban Car Family (EUCF) for the first time as a complete lineup at the Paris Motor Show. This family includes the CUPRA Raval, Volkswagen ID. Polo, Škoda Epiq, and Volkswagen ID. Cross, all built on the MEB+ Platform.

The initiative aims to make electric mobility more accessible to a broader customer base. The Brand Group Core, led by SEAT & CUPRA, has pooled the expertise of its brands to create four distinct models with a shared technological foundation, targeting the growing European small car segment.

Production of the EUCF models is based in Spain, with the CUPRA Raval and Volkswagen ID. Polo being manufactured in Martorell, and the Škoda Epiq and Volkswagen ID. Cross produced in Pamplona. This strategy leverages common components and technologies, with over 80 percent of parts being identical across the models.

The project is part of a significant investment in electric mobility in Spain, with SEAT & CUPRA, Brand Group Core, PowerCo, and partners investing ten billion euros. This includes investments in battery cell and battery system production facilities.

Customer interest in the Electric Urban Car Family has been strong, with nearly 150,000 orders received even before deliveries have begun. This response indicates a demand for affordable electric vehicles that combine modern technology with practical everyday use and distinct brand identities.

articles.headline: EV4EU Project Concludes, Advancing Bidirectional EV Charging Technology
articles.dek: Four-year EU project EV4EU finishes, delivering a bidirectional CCS charging prototype and open-source software to support electric vehicles in grid stabilization.
articles.lead: The European Union's EV4EU project has completed its four-year initiative focused on advancing bidirectional charging technology for electric vehicles. The project successfully developed a prototype for bidirectional charging using the CCS standard, enabling electric cars to both draw power from and supply it back to the grid.
articles.takeaway: Four-year EU project EV4EU finishes, delivering a bidirectional CCS charging prototype and open-source software to support electric vehicles in grid stabilization.
body: The European Union's EV4EU project has completed its four-year initiative focused on advancing bidirectional charging technology for electric vehicles. The project successfully developed a prototype for bidirectional charging using the CCS standard, enabling electric cars to both draw power from and supply it back to the grid.

In addition to the hardware prototype, the EV4EU project created open-source software specifically designed for charging point operators. This software aims to facilitate the integration and management of bidirectional charging capabilities within existing infrastructure.

The project culminated in four demonstration projects that showcased the practical applications of electric vehicles in enhancing the adaptability of the power system. These demonstrations highlighted how EVs can play a crucial role in stabilizing the electricity grid by managing energy flow.
The EV4EU initiative represents a significant step forward in the integration of electric vehicles into the broader energy landscape, moving beyond simple charging to active grid participation.

attribution.originalTitle: EV4EU project advances bidirectional charging

faqs.answer: The EV4EU project concluded by developing a bidirectional CCS charging prototype and open-source software for charging point operators.

faqs.answer: Electric cars can contribute to the adaptability of the power system by enabling bidirectional charging, allowing them to supply power back to the grid.

Germany is notably participating in this round, with eight of the selected projects based within the country. The focus on these specific minerals underscores their importance in the ongoing transition towards electric mobility and renewable energy storage.

This move by the EU Commission is part of a broader strategy to reduce reliance on external sources for these vital components. By investing in domestic and regional projects, the EU aims to strengthen its industrial base and ensure a stable supply chain for key technologies.

The selected projects are expected to contribute to the extraction, processing, and recycling of these critical raw materials, fostering innovation and job creation within the member states involved. The initiative aligns with the EU's goals for a green and digital transition.

articles.headline: United Dairy Farmers to Install EV Fast Chargers at Ohio Stores
articles.dek: The convenience store chain is adding DC fast chargers to six locations, aiming to support EV drivers while offering its usual amenities.
articles.lead: United Dairy Farmers (UDF), a family-owned chain, is integrating DC fast chargers for electric vehicles into six of its 170 Ohio stores. The first chargers are expected to be operational in early 2027. These new charging facilities will be located in stores that already provide food, indoor and outdoor seating, and Wi-Fi.
articles.takeaway: The convenience store chain is adding DC fast chargers to six locations, aiming to support EV drivers while offering its usual amenities.
body: United Dairy Farmers (UDF), a family-owned chain, is integrating DC fast chargers for electric vehicles into six of its 170 Ohio stores. The first chargers are expected to be operational in early 2027. These new charging facilities will be located in stores that already provide food, indoor and outdoor seating, and Wi-Fi.

UDF has secured National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) funding for these six locations, which are situated in Greater Cincinnati and Columbus. The company applied for NEVI funding for all six sites and was awarded the grants. The specific charging speeds, connector types, and pricing details have not yet been released.

The chargers are anticipated to be Electric Era's 400-kW models, designed to meet Ohio's NEVI guidelines. Electric Era's technology utilizes a combination of grid electricity and on-site batteries to manage peak demand and facilitate charging in areas with limited grid capacity.

Customers will have the option to use U-Drive Plus loyalty credits towards charging costs and can earn additional credits through qualifying purchases at the stores. UDF plans to announce individual opening dates for the chargers and will use customer demand and feedback to guide future expansion plans.

attribution.originalTitle: Ice cream and EV fast charging? United Dairy Farmers is bringing both to Ohio

faqs.question: Where will the new EV fast chargers be located?
faqs.answer: The new EV fast chargers will be installed at six United Dairy Farmers store locations in Hilliard, Lebanon, Mason, Maineville, and two in Cincinnati.

faqs.question: What technology will the EV fast chargers use?
faqs.answer: The chargers are expected to be Electric Era's 400-kW models, which combine grid electricity with on-site batteries to support charging.
